origins.section: 12.1 A Key Holds a Queue: `out` Adds, `put` Replaces, `push` Goes First
12.2 A Wait Without a Timeout and an Entry Without a Lease Both Last Forever
12.4 A Listener Runs on the Writer's Thread and Takes Nothing
12.5 A Transient Space Hands Back the Stored Object, and a Persistent One a Copy

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-failover-mode: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-failover-mode: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-failover-mode: 12.1 shows push after three midnights: participants read the newest date (1108) while the key holds 4 entries, so push gives the latest mode and piles up an entry per switch.
recorded.prompt:q-undeploy: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-undeploy: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-undeploy: 12.2 shows the untimed worker still alive after undeploy and handling a queued job, and says a redeploy would start a second consumer beside the old one, so either may take it.
recorded.prompt:q-audit-listener: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-listener: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-listener: 12.4 shows the slow listener running on the writer's thread (in a server, the QServer session inside IncomingListener), delaying every answer by its sleep.
recorded.prompt:q-velocity-count: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-velocity-count: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-velocity-count: 12.5 says je: builds a new copy on every read, so a change reaches only the copy (the stored MTI stayed 0220), while tspace: hands back the stored object, which is why the tests pass; the stored count therefore never moves.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-failover-mode:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-failover-mode:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-failover-mode:b: 12.1 says only put replaces the whole list and shows push leaving 4 entries under the key.
recorded.prompt:q-failover-mode:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-failover-mode:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-failover-mode:c: 12.1 says push inserts at the head and readers get the head, and its push output reads the newest date; but the same section says of out that 'rdp returns the oldest entry', so the option's reason is partly true as worded.
recorded.prompt:q-failover-mode:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-failover-mode:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-failover-mode:d: 12.1 says push goes first (inserts at the head), not behind, and shows 4 entries rather than one.
recorded.prompt:q-undeploy:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-undeploy:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-undeploy:a: 12.2 says clearing running changes nothing for a thread waiting inside in, and shows the thread alive after undeploy.
recorded.prompt:q-undeploy:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-undeploy:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-undeploy:b: 12.2 shows 'job-worker thread alive after undeploy: true', so Q2 did not end the wait, though the page never states outright that Q2 does not interrupt.
recorded.prompt:q-undeploy:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-undeploy:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-undeploy:d: 12.1 and the 12.7 table say in takes the head, so one consumer removes the entry; the page does not spell out the two-waiter case explicitly.
recorded.prompt:q-audit-listener:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-listener:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-listener:b: 12.4 attributes the delay to the listener running inside out on the writer's thread, not to the TransactionManager waiting; the page does not say explicitly that the TM ignores listeners.
recorded.prompt:q-audit-listener:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-listener:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-listener:c: 12.4 states TSpace calls listeners on the writer's thread, one after another, and the output shows it ran on main.
recorded.prompt:q-audit-listener:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-listener:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-listener:d: 12.4 says the listener is told about an entry that stays in the space and runs synchronously in the writer's call, with answers 300 ms slower.
recorded.prompt:q-velocity-count:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-velocity-count:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-velocity-count:a: 12.5 says only tspace: hands back the stored object; je: hands back a new copy ('read == stored: false').
recorded.prompt:q-velocity-count:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-velocity-count:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-velocity-count:b: 12.5 says to change a clone and write it back yourself with put or push, which implies nothing writes the copy back automatically; the page never says so outright, so this is inferred.
recorded.prompt:q-velocity-count:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-velocity-count:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-velocity-count:d: 12.5 says the only thing je: refuses is a non-Serializable value on write; the stored advice stays 0220 because the change went to a copy, not because je: refused it.
